title: Write a Test Plan a Mentor Would Actually Sign Off On
objective: Write and defend a test plan for a real, nontrivial upcoming change, covering scope, risk, test layers, quality gates, and what would make you, not just a tool, confident enough to ship.
whyThisMatters: This is the artifact that separates someone who can write tests from someone who can be trusted to decide what testing a real change needs, which is the skill this curriculum has been building toward.
evidence: The written test plan, naming risks, layers, gates applied/skipped and explicit exclusions
Commits implementing the highest-risk tests from the plan, passing
A record of the plan review and what changed as a result of it
acceptanceCriteria: The plan names specific risks for this specific change, not a generic checklist reused across changes.
The plan states which existing quality gates apply and which are explicitly skipped, with a reason for each.
At least 2 explicitly excluded test cases are named along with the reason for excluding them.
At least the top 2-3 highest-risk tests named in the plan are implemented and passing.
A record exists of at least one change made to the plan as a result of review.
